summaries.information_need: A researcher wants to know how a lag structure that is fixed and arbitrary limits a time-varying variance equation, and more broadly why more flexible variance models are needed for economic and financial time series data, especially given the non-negativity constraints that estimated parameters must satisfy in practice.

A researcher wants a full specification of the GARCH process, whose current variance depends on both past squared shocks and its own past values, together with a rigorous proof of the parameter condition under which such a process is stationary with finite variance.
summaries.answer_type: model specification with formal stationarity proof

summaries.information_need: A researcher wants the precise parameter condition under which higher-order moments of a simple conditionally heteroskedastic process exist, together with a rigorous derivation establishing that condition and showing how it generalizes the analogous existence condition already known for the simpler ARCH case.

A researcher wants the coefficient of kurtosis implied by a simple conditionally heteroskedastic process, and whether its implied distribution is heavier-tailed than normal, together with how the process's memory can be summarized through its mean and median lag, measures useful for comparing how quickly different fitted specifications forget past shocks.
summaries.answer_type: derivation of distributional and persistence properties

summaries.information_need: An analyst wants to know how the autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation functions of the squared series behave under this class of volatility models, useful for identifying appropriate lag orders from sample data, together with how the general moment-existence condition specializes to particular model orders.

A practitioner wants the maximum likelihood estimator for a regression model whose error variance follows a volatility process, including its score and information-matrix structure, together with a practical iterative algorithm for computing it and the estimator's asymptotic distribution.

A practitioner wants a formal Lagrange multiplier test for whether time-varying volatility is present in a regression model's errors, together with an understanding of when such a test breaks down or fails to distinguish between competing lag specifications sharing the same alternative hypothesis.

An analyst wants a model comparison between competing volatility specifications fitted to a macroeconomic time series, judging fit through residual diagnostics, tail-shape statistics, and the persistence and width of the resulting forecast intervals across calm and turbulent periods, to see if the added complexity pays off.
